body.p: 1.A propulsor assembly for an aircraft, the propulsor assembly comprising:a propulsor connected to the aircraft; anda cyclic control assembly, wherein the cyclic control assembly comprises:an actuator, wherein the actuator is an electric actuator; anda push rod, wherein:the push rod is mechanically connected to the actuator and the propulsor;the push rod is configured to increase a blade angle of the propulsor when the push rod is displaced in a first direction; and the push rod is configured to decrease the blade angle of the propulsor when the push rod is displaced in a second direction.
body.br:
SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.1170.0932. The propulsor assembly of claim 1, further comprising an electric motor, the electric motor comprising a stator and a rotor, wherein the rotor is mechanically connected to the propulsor;
and wherein:
the propulsor is mechanically connected to the rotor using a shaft, wherein the shaft includes a proximal end and a distal end mechanically coupled to the propulsor;
the shaft has a central lumen running from the proximal end to the distal end; and
the pushrod extends at least partially through the central lumen.
3. The propulsor assembly of claim 2, wherein the pushrod runs parallel to a rotational axis of the rotor of the electric motor.
4. The propulsor assembly of claim 1, wherein the cyclic control assembly further comprises a swashplate rocker, wherein the swashplate rocker mechanically connects the push rod and the actuator.
5. The propulsor assembly of claim 4, wherein the swashplate rocker is configured to:
translate movement by the actuator in a first actuation direction into movement of the pushrod in the first direction; and
translate movement by the actuator in a second actuation direction into movement of the pushrod in the second direction.
6. The propulsor assembly of claim 1, wherein the cyclic control assembly further comprises a propulsor rocker, wherein the propulsor rocker is mechanically connected to the push rod and the propulsor.
7. The propulsor assembly of claim 6, wherein the propulsor rocker is configured to:
translate movement by the pushrod in the first direction to an increase in the blade angle of the propulsor; and
translate movement by the pushrod in the second direction to a decrease in the blade angle of the propulsor.
8. The propulsor assembly of claim 6, further comprising a propulsor link, wherein:
the propulsor rocker comprises a first propulsor rocker end and a second propulsor rocker end;
the second propulsor rocker end is attached to the push rod; and
the first propulsor rocker end is attached to the propulsor link.
9. The propulsor assembly of claim 1, further comprising a flight controller, wherein:
the flight controller is communicatively connected to the actuator; and
the flight controller is configured to:
command the actuator to increase the blade angle of the propulsor; and
command the actuator to decrease the blade angle of the propulsor.
10. The propulsor assembly of claim 1, wherein the propulsor comprises a monolithic propulsor.
11. The propulsor assembly of claim 1, wherein the propulsor comprises:a hub, wherein the hub is mechanically connected to a shaft; and
a plurality of blades, wherein each of the plurality of blades are connected to and extend outward from the hub.
12. The propulsor assembly of claim 1, wherein the plurality of blades comprises two blades.
13. The propulsor assembly of claim 1, further comprising:A first electric motor, the first electric motor comprising a first stator and a rotor, wherein the rotor is mechanically connected to the propulsor; and
a second electric motor, wherein the second electric motor comprises a second stator.
14. The propulsor assembly of claim 1, further comprising a flap mechanism mechanically connected to the propulsor, wherein the flap mechanism is configured to allow the propulsor to rotate about a pivot point of the flap mechanism.
15. The propulsor assembly of claim 14, further comprising an electric motor, the electric motor comprising a stator and a rotor, wherein the rotor is mechanically connected to the propulsor;and wherein the flap mechanism comprises:
a base rotatably attached to an aircraft and configured to rotate about a rotational axis,
wherein the rotor of the electric motor is configured to rotate about the rotational axis;
and
a hinge, wherein the hinge connects the base and the propulsor and is configured to allow the propulsor to rotate about the pivot point of the flap mechanism.
16. The propulsor assembly of claim 14, wherein the flap mechanism is configured to passively control in-flight transients.
17. The propulsor assembly of claim 15, wherein the flap mechanism further comprises a locking mechanism comprising a plurality of springs.
18. The propulsor assembly of claim 17, wherein each spring of the plurality of springs is attached to the base of the flap mechanism and the propulsor.
19. The propulsor assembly of claim 1, wherein the cyclic control assembly comprises a second actuator, wherein the second actuator is mechanically connected to the pushrod and configured to rotate the pushrod about a transverse axis.
20. The propulsor assembly of claim 1, further comprising:a flight controller; and
a plurality of pilot controls, wherein:
the flight controller is communicatively connected to the plurality of pilot controls;
and the first actuator is mechanically disconnected from the plurality of flight controls.
